job.title: Head of Campaigns, Community and Influence
job.description:
What would it look like to help put women's rights at the forefront of the national conversation? To turn powerful evidence into campaigns that demand change, galvanise communities and make decision-makers sit up and listen?

This is an exciting opportunity to do exactly that.

With a remarkable 150-year heritage, this ambitious women's rights charity is ready for its next chapter. Determined to shake things up, raise its profile and challenge the status quo, the organisation wants to become an even bolder and more influential force in advancing women's rights and tackling misogyny across the UK.

As Head of Campaigns, Community and Influence, you'll lead this ambition. This is a brand-new leadership role, offering the opportunity to shape the organisation's campaigning strategy, connect public affairs with digital campaigning and community engagement, and build the foundations of a movement that brings women together to drive change.

The charity has a strong history of influencing MPs, ministers and policymakers. Now, it wants to go further: building its digital presence, creating opportunities for women to share their experiences, and mobilising communities to campaign for vital legal and policy reform. This is a senior campaigning role, focused on how to drive community-engagement throughout all its work.

The role
Reporting to the CEO, you'll lead a team of five across public affairs, investigative research, content and campaigns, AI and community building. You'll bring these specialisms together, providing strategic direction and ensuring the organisation's work is bold, joined-up and influential.

You'll develop campaigns that cut through, build an engaged and active community, grow the charity's profile as a political voice and ensure its influence is felt both online and in the corridors of power.

There is an exciting agenda ahead, including:
  • Closing the gender pay gap and securing greater protections for women at work.
  • Championing self-employed women and those working in the platform economy.
  • Improving awareness and support for women's health in the workplace.
  • Driving legal and policy reform around gender and AI.
  • Exploring how online spaces and the 'femosphere' are shaping women's experiences.

About you
You'll be a strategic, politically astute and creative campaigner, with the ambition and conviction to help take an established organisation into its next chapter.
  • Demonstrable experience leading campaigns, advocacy or movement-building to achieve social, political or cultural change.
  • Experience mobilising communities and people with lived experience to create meaningful collective action.
  • A track record of influencing decision-makers and translating evidence and policy into compelling public campaigns.
  • Experience developing digital engagement and campaigning approaches to grow awareness and build momentum.
  • Previous line management experience and an inclusive, values-led approach to leading and developing teams.

Above all, you'll have a genuine passion for gender equality, a curious and innovative mindset, and the confidence to challenge convention. You'll be excited by the opportunity to build something, try new approaches and help make women's rights impossible to ignore.

What's on offer?
  • £55,000–£60,000 FTE.
  • Permanent, 4 days per week (5 days considered). Flexible working hours.
  • Remote working in the UK - London and Westminster presence required approximately 5-6 times per month.
  • 36 days' annual leave (inclusive of bank holidays). Enhanced maternity and sickness pay. Regular team away days and collaborative working.

First-stage interviews: Online, w/c 14 December. 2nd stage in person.

job.title: Finance Manager
job.description:
Are you an experienced Finance Manager with a strong background in charity sector finance and excellent technical accounting skills? Available for your next interim assignment and ready to hit the ground running?

£24.75 per hour PAYE | Remote | Up to 3 Months
Start date: Monday 30 November 2026

This is a hands-on role offering the opportunity to take ownership of UK finance operations, support senior leadership and work closely with colleagues across an international finance function.

Key responsibilities
Reporting to the Finance Director, you will:
  • Manage UK month-end and year-end processes, including balance sheet reconciliations.
  • Prepare monthly management accounts, financial analysis and reporting for senior leadership.
  • Coordinate budgets and forecasts, working closely with budget holders.
  • Prepare UK statutory accounts, audit schedules and supporting documentation.
  • Coordinate external audits and support consolidated audit requirements.

  • Review transactions, invoices, expenses, payments and intercompany reconciliations, ensuring robust financial controls.

About you
You will be a technically strong, hands-on finance professional with proven experience working within the charity or not-for-profit sector. You must be confident applying UK charity accounting requirements, working independently and managing competing deadlines.

  • Previous experience working within a charity or not-for-profit organisation.

  • Experience with balance sheet reconciliations, audit preparation and financial controls.
  • Experience overseeing payroll and workplace pension processes.
  • Advanced Excel skills, including PivotTables, SUMIFS and VLOOKUP or equivalent.

job.title: Chief Officer
job.description:
Could you help older people live more independent, connected and fulfilling lives?

Join Age Concern Epsom & Ewell as our next Chief Officer and help shape the future of a much-loved local charity, ensuring older people across the community can access the support, advice and connections they need to thrive.

Location: Epsom & Ewell, Surrey (office-based at The Old Town Hall, Epsom, with some home working possible)
Salary: £50,000 - £55,000 FTE (based on a 37 hour week)
Contract: Permanent, part time (32 hours per week)

About Age Concern Epsom & Ewell
Founded in 1947, Age Concern Epsom & Ewell is an independent local charity helping older people navigate later life, maintain their independence and enjoy better wellbeing. Our services include information and advice, medical transport, befriending, home visiting, IT support, DIY assistance and social activities, helping people access practical support and remain connected to their community.

Our work is delivered by nine part-time staff, supported by a dedicated volunteer network. In the past year, the quality of our services was recognised when our volunteer community was nominated for The King's Award for Voluntary Service. From helping people access information and advice, to providing companionship and transport to medical appointments, our work makes a tangible difference to everyday lives.

As we approach our 80th anniversary in 2027, demand for support is growing alongside the challenges of an ageing population. We need to strengthen our financial sustainability, review our services and resources, and adapt to changes in local government and partnership arrangements.

This is an opportunity to build on our strong community roots and long-standing relationships, ensuring the charity remains responsive, resilient and well placed to support older people for years to come.

As our next Chief Officer, you will:
  • Translate the charity’s strategy into practical plans, lead an initial organisational review and work with trustees to agree priorities, strengthen governance and build organisational resilience.
  • Oversee the charity’s day-to-day operations, finances and services, using evidence on costs, impact and community need to improve quality, efficiency and resource decisions.
  • Work with the fundraising team, legacy co-ordinator and trustees to strengthen existing income streams, develop new funding opportunities and support long-term financial sustainability.
  • Support and develop staff and volunteers, while building partnerships and raising awareness to extend the charity’s reach and ensure older people, families, funders and partners understand the support available.

Who you are
You will be a practical, thoughtful and motivated leader who combines strategic perspective with a willingness to get involved in the day-to-day running of a small charity. You will bring a warm, approachable and collaborative leadership style, with a genuine commitment to helping people and an appreciation of the personal, community-rooted nature of the charity.

You will bring:
  • Experience of leading people, services or an organisation and translating priorities into achievable plans.
  • Demonstrable experience of financial management, including budgeting, monitoring expenditure and making effective use of resources.
  • Experience of fundraising, income generation or developing funding opportunities.
  • Experience of managing or supporting staff and/or volunteers, with the ability to build an engaged and collaborative team.
  • The ability to assess organisational needs, review established practices and lead improvements and change constructively.
  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills, with the confidence to work effectively with trustees, colleagues, volunteers and external partners.
  • A genuine commitment to helping older people live independent, fulfilling and socially connected lives, alongside a responsible approach to the charity's long-term sustainability.
  • Knowledge of charity governance and the responsibilities involved in maintaining safe, well-managed services, including safeguarding and health and safety.

Experience in older people's services, advice, health, social care or community support would be desirable, as would experience of partnership working with local authorities, health services or other voluntary organisations.

Above all, you will be a self-starter who can identify what needs attention, ask the right questions and turn ideas into practical action. You will listen, build trust and bring people with you, balancing the confidence to lead with the judgement to involve others in shaping the charity's future.

For more information including details of how to apply, please download the appointment brief.

job.title: Deputy Play Manager
job.description:
Harris Hill is delighted to be partnering with a well-established children’s charity in London in their search for a Deputy Play Manager.

Full-time | £36,000 per annum

The charity has been supporting children, young people and families for over 25 years through a range of play, family support and youth programmes. Their Ofsted-registered after-school and holiday play schemes provide children aged 4–11 with safe, engaging and nurturing environments to explore, grow and thrive.

As Deputy Play Manager, you’ll play a key leadership role within the play service, helping to design, deliver and evaluate a high-quality programme of activities. You’ll support the Play Manager in day-to-day operations (including managing enquiries/collection of fees), team management and ensuring compliance with all safeguarding, health and safety, and Ofsted standards.

This is a hands-on role combining leadership, planning, and active delivery — you’ll work directly with children and families to create safe, inclusive, and stimulating play environments.

About you

Essential skills and experience:
  • Level 3 qualification (or above) in Playwork, Early Years, or a related field.
  • Minimum of three years’ experience working directly with children aged 4–11.
  • Strong understanding of EYFS and Ofsted requirements.
  • Experience planning and delivering engaging, age-appropriate play activities.
  • Confident leading active, outdoor or adventure-based play.
  • Sound understanding of safeguarding and child protection.
  • Excellent communication and team leadership skills.
  • Strong organisational and IT skills.

Desirable:
  • Experience supporting children with additional needs or from diverse backgrounds.
  • Experience supervising others or managing volunteers.
  • Knowledge of current issues affecting children and families.
  • Relevant training such as paediatric first aid or food hygiene.

Play is at the heart of what they do — the organisation believes that every child deserves the opportunity to enjoy a happy, fulfilling childhood through both free and guided play experiences.

If you’re passionate about play, child development and helping young people thrive, we’d love to hear from you.

For more information, please submit your CV to lizzy.clark@harrishill.co.uk

Please note, CVs are being reviewed on a rolling basis, and only successful applicants will be contacted with more information.

job.title: Fundraising Manager
job.description:
﻿Harris Hill is delighted to be partnering with Wintercomfort, who provide support to people who are homeless, at risk of homelessness or who have a history of homelessness. They are searching for a Fundraising Manager to join their team.

As Fundraising Manager, you will be responsible for developing and delivering fundraising activities across corporate partnerships, individual giving, major donors, community fundraising, legacies and events.

Working closely with the CEO and Finance Manager, you will develop a three-year income generation strategy and annual fundraising plans aligned with organisational objectives.

You will build and manage income pipelines, monitor performance, while identifying new opportunities to grow income and maximise existing fundraising streams.

You will develop long-term partnerships through sponsorship, employee fundraising, matched giving and gifts in kind and create compelling, tailored proposals and pitches to attract and secure support from a range of donors.

You will also plan and deliver engaging fundraising events, provide excellent donor stewardship and oversee donor administration.

To be considered for this role you will need:
  • Proven track record of developing and delivering income generation strategies that meet or exceed target.
  • Experience of using pipelines and budget management to achieve fundraising targets.
  • Experience of leading, developing and managing fundraising relationships with individuals, understanding the needs and expectations of donors and supporters.
  • Experience of securing and developing corporate partnerships and delivering successful fundraising events.

If this role sounds of interest to you and you want to have a chat and review the full job description, please do contact Dominic at Harris Hill on dominic.gilchrist@harrishill.co.uk or call him on 020 7820 7332

Permanent, full-time (part-time also considered)
Location: Cambridge with hybrid working

job.title: Chief Executive Officer
job.description:
**NB: This job has now expired and appears for reference only, but please get in touch if you are interested in similar positions.

Harris Hill is delighted to be working with Citizens Advice St Albans District (CASTAD) to recruit its new Chief Executive Officer.

CASTAD provides free, confidential, impartial and independent advice to help people overcome their problems. We campaign on the issues that matter to them when their voices need to be heard.

We want to see a world where no one suffers through ignorance of their rights and responsibilities, or an inability to pursue them; and where the underlying causes of people’s problems have been eliminated.

As Chief Executive, you will:

  • Deliver high-quality client services to approximately 9,000 users per annum.
  • Ensure financial resources are in place to run the service.
  • Work with the Trustee Board to define and lead the future strategy and sustainability of CASTAD.
  • Execute the agreed strategy by ensuring a detailed and measurable Business Plan is in place, regularly tracked, and reported on.

If you are inspired and excited by what CASTAD does, we’d love to hear from you.

job.title: Chief Executive Officer
job.description:
**NB: This job has now expired and appears for reference only, but please get in touch if you are interested in similar positions.

Could you lead a charity with deep roots and a strong sense of community into its next chapter – creating greater opportunities for people with disabilities and/or neurodiversity to thrive?

Location: White Lodge, Chertsey, KT16 0FA (hybrid, minimum 3 days a week in the office)
Salary: circa £75,000
Contract: Permanent, full time, 37.5 hours per week

About us
White Lodge is a leading charity supporting children, young people and adults with disabilities and their families. With more than 60 years’ history, we support over 2,500 people across Surrey and beyond through specialist services and facilities in Chertsey.

White Lodge is a community as much as a service provider, built around our values of ENABLE: Equity, Nurture, Advocacy, Belonging, Language and Empathy. Our Active Plan 2025–30 sets four ambitions: Enhance accessibility and social opportunities; Champion customers' voices in health and social care; Transform local attitudes; and Strengthen its resources.

With strong systems, governance and a diversified income base, White Lodge is well placed for its next phase. The new CEO will provide continuity while bringing strategic, operational and entrepreneurial leadership to respond to a changing funding environment and pursue new opportunities, including a children's services tender.

As our next Chief Executive Officer, you will:
  • Strategy & Impact: Deliver White Lodge's strategy, translating ambitions into measurable outcomes and impact.
  • Leadership: Lead and develop a committed workforce, fostering an inclusive, accountable and values-led culture.
  • Governance & Finance: Partner with the Board to ensure strong governance, financial sustainability and effective risk management.
  • Operations: Ensure high-quality, person-centred services and effective organisational systems and performance.
  • Income & Partnerships: Diversify income and develop relationships with commissioners, funders, NHS partners and the wider community.
  • Influence & Advocacy: Champion customers' voices, strengthen White Lodge's profile and help transform attitudes towards disability.
  • Safeguarding & Compliance: Ensure high standards of safeguarding, regulatory compliance, equality and ethical leadership.

Who you are
  • A seasoned senior leader with significant experience in a complex organisation, ideally within charity, health, care or wider public services.
  • Experienced in leading substantial teams and complex services, with strong financial, operational and commercial understanding.
  • A strategic thinker with a track record of organisational change, sustainable growth and measurable outcomes.
  • Experienced in working effectively with a Board, commissioners, funders and strategic partners.
  • An emotionally intelligent, inclusive and entrepreneurial leader who builds trust, creates clarity and brings people with them.
  • A compelling communicator and ambassador, committed to equity, inclusion, dignity, safeguarding and ensuring lived experience shapes decisions.
  • Experience of disability, social care, children's services or another regulated service environment would be advantageous, as would commissioned services or significant tender experience. Previous CEO experience is desirable but not essential; exceptional Directors or Deputy CEOs ready to step up are encouraged to apply.

Why White Lodge?
  • Help create a world that is inclusive to all, regardless of ability.
  • Lead an established charity with a committed team, strong systems and strengthened governance.
  • Deliver the ambitions of the Active Plan 2025–30 and pursue new opportunities.
  • Work alongside customers, families, staff, volunteers and trustees who share White Lodge's values.

Application
